The tenth anniversary of the 2016 South China Sea arbitration ruling saw 14 nations, led by Japan and the U.S., issue a joint statement declaring China's claims legally baseless. China dismissed the statement as a 'farce' and accused Japan of having no standing. Meanwhile, a Chinese submarine-launched ballistic missile test was flagged as a significant signal, and the J-16 'Beast Mode' display reinforced Beijing's conventional deterrence.

## 海军与印太 · 8 items

Naval and Indo-Pacific developments cover three main threads: the ongoing Strait of Hormuz crisis and its impact on shipping, major arms production increases (U.S. LRASM/JASSM, EU hypersonic interceptor), and force modernization (German Navy laser weapon, anti-drone warfare, RIMPAC exercises). The U.S. Navy also issued a new medical shaving waiver policy, while a Congressional report details extended nuclear deterrence. 

- Despite Iranian attacks, Strait of Hormuz transits doubled from May to June 2026 (to 576), but remain a fraction of pre-crisis levels (3,131 in June 2025) ([USNI News](https://news.usni.org/2026/07/10/hormuz-sees-traffic-bump-despite-ongoing-iranian-attacks)). The shipping industry is adjusting to high-risk operations.
- The U.S. Air Force plans to triple LRASM and JASSM production, with a planned procurement of over 11,000 missiles over five to seven years ([Naval News](https://www.navalnews.com/naval-news/2026/07/lrasm-and-jassm-production-to-triple-under-new-us-air-force-contract/)). This dramatically expands the Pentagon's inventory for long-range anti-ship and strike capabilities.
- The EU signed a grant for the MBDA-led HYDIS hypersonic interceptor project, launching a three-year concept phase for the AQUILA interceptor ([Naval News](https://www.navalnews.com/naval-news/2026/07/eu-signs-grant-for-mbda-led-hydis-hypersonic-interceptor-project/)). This addresses the growing hypersonic threat.
- The German Navy selected MBDA and Rheinmetall to develop a high-energy laser weapon, with deployment expected by 2029 ([Naval News](https://www.navalnews.com/naval-news/2026/07/german-navy-to-deploy-new-mbda-and-rheinmetall-laser-weapon-by-2029/)). This marks a step toward directed-energy naval air defense.
- A report on anti-drone warfare at sea emphasizes the need for AESA radar and hard-kill effectors to counter Tier 2 drone threats ([Naval News](https://www.navalnews.com/naval-news/2026/07/anti-drone-warfare-at-sea-matching-sensors-and-effectors-to-the-threat/)).
- RIMPAC 2026 is now in its at-sea phase, with live-firing drills including Canadian frigates ([USNI News](https://news.usni.org/2026/07/10/usni-news-western-pacific-pulse-july-10-2026)). 
- A Congressional Research Service report on U.S. extended deterrence and regional nuclear capabilities was released, highlighting assurance to over 30 allies ([USNI News](https://news.usni.org/2026/07/10/report-to-congress-on-u-s-extended-deterrence-and-regional-nuclear-capabilities-2)).

**Signal:** The U.S. is massively investing in long-range standoff missiles, while European navies focus on hypersonic and laser defenses—indicating a shift away from short-range systems toward distributed, longer-range engagements in a contested maritime environment.
